evals.name: phase1-block-ambiguous-feature
evals.prompt: Add a caching layer to the Context Synapse embedding lookup.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 fires. Request is ambiguous (cache strategy, invalidation policy, TTL, memory vs disk, async boundary implications are all unspecified). Claude stops before writing code and outputs a surgical clarifying question list. No design or implementation is produced.

evals.name: full-gate-deterministic-feature
evals.prompt: In the Secure Pride RADIUS auth module, add a function that checks whether a given certificate serial number appears in the CRL before allowing authentication. The CRL is already loaded as a list of strings at startup. Return a boolean. Log rejected serials using the existing masked-identifier logger.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 passes silently (fully specified). Phase 2 produces minimal design: single pure function, no new dependencies. Phase 3 targets only the auth module. Phase 4 produces a verification block with concrete success criteria (e.g., assert revoked serial returns False, assert valid serial returns True, assert masked log entry is written on rejection).

evals.name: bypass-trivial-fix

evals.expected_output: Gates are bypassed entirely. Claude ships the rename directly without any phase headers, clarifying questions, or verification block. No gating overhead.

evals.name: exclusion-creative-posture

evals.name: phase1-silent-pass-spec-provided-inline
evals.prompt: Here's the full spec for the password hashing upgrade: use argon2id with m=65536, t=3, p=4. Input is a plaintext string, output is the encoded hash. No migration of existing hashes needed — new passwords only. Add it as a single pure function `hash_password(plaintext: str) -> str` in `auth/hashing.py`. That's everything.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 passes silently. The spec is complete: algorithm, parameters, I/O contract, scope target, and migration exclusion are all explicit in the message. No clarifying questions. Claude proceeds directly to Phase 2 minimal design.
